title: Nutty Malaysian Pork Tenderloin Satay
description: A cultured and bouncy Malaysian dish featuring pork tenderloin, ferment-kimchi, and satvik-friendly ingredients, perfect for crowds. This recipe combines the flavors of Malaysia with a twist of spicy kimchi.
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat, about 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a blender, combine peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger, and blend until smooth.
Place the pork tenderloin in a large ziplock bag and pour the peanut sauce over it, turning to coat.
Seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Remove the pork from the marinade and thread onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill the satay for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, or until cooked through to an internal temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit.
Meanwhile, heat the kimchi in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Serve the satay with the spicy kimchi sauce spooned over the top.
Garnish with chopped peanuts and fresh cilantro, if desired.
